$comment: game-factory's task format, GameTask (game-task/1): one task a game ships with, on its orphan tasks branch (Tasks/<name>.json) and, split into the agent's and the grader's parts, in its dataset. The deterministic `probe` check kind is described for task authors in docs/task-probes.md, and every task is seeded; a build check's `fails_at_start` marks a start that doesn't compile. tools/validate-game.py checks every task in a game repo's tasks branch and in a dataset against this schema and the rules it cannot express. Since 2026-11-11 (Lab game grader 1.5.0) a task play may turn the mouse wheel (`wheel`), move the mouse (`move`) and stage a contact (`pin`, `damage`, `set`); an actor select may filter by a reflected property (`where`) or leave the player out (`player` false); a probe may read the world's lowest time dilation and pause (`world`), an actor's short stops, montage, damage taken and AI focus (`frozen`, `montage`, `damage_taken`, `focus_player`), and the sounds that start (`started`, `started_audible`, `sounds`, `repeats`, a select `near` a point). Since 2026-11-12 (Lab game grader 1.7.0) a task play may name the task plays that run before it on the same side (`after`), for a play that reads what another writes.

ActionsJudge.description:
A reviewer's question over what the agent did, from its own trace: each tool call in order (the tool, its
arguments and what it returned, cut), whether it worked, and which made a checkpoint; never the agent's reasoning
or messages. How the game was made counts beside the game itself (the owner, 2026-10-14: grade "based on agent
actions, and the final build").
ActionsJudge.title: ActionsJudge

AssetMeasure.description:
The project as saved, read in a headless editor pass: an asset's property (`asset` + prop:<path>), or actors
of a map (`map` + `select`).
AssetMeasure.title: AssetMeasure

AtCamera.description: The player's camera, `forward` cm along its view.
AtCamera.title: AtCamera

AtXYZ.description: A fixed point in the world (cm).
AtXYZ.title: AtXYZ

AudioMeasure.description:
What the player hears (probes.md 2d): the sounds playing that `select` matches, each at its volume at the
listener (its own volume, its class's and mixes', times its distance and occlusion attenuation; the output's
master volume left out): `count` (how many), `audible` (how many at 0.001, -60 dB, or louder), `volume` (their sum),
`max_volume` (the loudest). A play with an audio measure runs with sound (muted). The volumes' threshold is
calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (_probe).

The sounds that start (docs/planning/2026-11-11_game-grader-audio/spec.md), every one however short, seen once a
frame: `started` (how many started in each sample's interval, summed over the samples picked by default),
`started_audible` (how many became audible at the listener, counted in the interval where they first did), each
start selected once, at the sample after it (so never by `owner`), and from the starts'
own names in the order they started, over the samples picked: `sounds` (how many different sound assets),
`repeats` (how many started with the same sound as the start just before them). `sounds` and `repeats` read
nothing when a start's sound was made at run time (a procedural wave has no name to tell it by); they take no
`agg`.
AudioMeasure.title: AudioMeasure

AudioSelect.description:
The sounds playing (probes.md 2d): by the sound asset's name (`sound`, a wildcard), its sound class's or a parent
class's name (`sound_class`, a wildcard), an owner actor the `owner` select matches, and `near` a point (a sound
played at a place: where it plays, or for the started fields where it started; a sound with no place, 2D or
unspatialized, is near nothing); none: every sound (2026-11-11_game-grader-audio/spec.md).
AudioSelect.title: AudioSelect

Axis.description: An axis event (MouseX, MouseY, Gamepad_LeftX) with its value, e.g. mouse look.
Axis.title: Axis

Boot.description: The game starts (headless, rendering offscreen) and runs `seconds` with no crash and no fatal error in its log.
Boot.title: Boot

Build.description:
The editor target compiles. `fails_at_start`: the task's start doesn't build, and making it build is the task
(a compile error the engine rejects); the start is never played, so nothing in the task may need it played
(docs/task-probes.md, section 3.1; tools/validate-game.py).
Build.title: Build

Calibrate.description: Threshold s + f * (r - s): the start (s) and the developers' fix (r) measured in the grading environment.
Calibrate.title: Calibrate

Click.description:
A click on the first visible button widget of that name or class, as a player would: a UMG button by its name or
class, else a Slate button (a game's own `SNew(SButton)` UI) by its text, tag or type, names and captions compared
alike in lower case with every run of other characters one `_` ("New_expedition" clicks a button reading "New
expedition"), pressed at its centre through Slate (probes.md 2m). A click no button takes is a miss the play
reports.
Click.title: Click

CodeJudge.description:
A code reviewer's question over the run's own change (its diff from the start, text files) beside the game's
real change for the same problem (the seed's `reference`, a bug's fix from the game's history), which the agent
never sees.
CodeJudge.title: CodeJudge

ComponentSelect.description:
Registered components of a class (NiagaraComponent, DecalComponent, AudioComponent), optionally of an owner
actor the `owner` select matches, near a point, of a mesh component's mesh asset (`mesh`, a wildcard), and
`visible`: only the components drawn (as the `visible` field reads them); `effect`: only live effects, whatever
made them (a particle system, Niagara or Cascade, that is active; a decal that is drawn; an effect actor by its
component), with or without `class` (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5).
ComponentSelect.title: ComponentSelect

ComponentsMeasure.description:
Registered components (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5): `x`, `y`, `z` and `speed` (cm/s: its physics
body's while it simulates, else its own velocity, else how far it moved since the previous sample) of a scene
component; `extent_x|y|z` (its world bounds' half-size) and `simulating` (its physics, a skeletal mesh's any body)
of a primitive; `intensity` and `on` (it lights the scene: visible, not hidden in game, its owner not hidden, an
intensity above 0) of a light; `changed` (1 when the primitive differs from the first sample it was seen in: hidden
or shown, its world bounds moved, a skinned mesh's pose moved), `bounds_change` and `pose_change` (cm, the amounts
behind it); `lit` (1 when it gives off light: a light that lights the scene, or a drawn mesh whose material is
emissive or unlit and bright, read from its material graph where that evaluates whole and else as rendered) and
`glow` (how much, one amount over every kind of source, particle systems among them; docs/task-probes.md, sections 2.4 and 2.5), the
way to check for light whatever a build made it with; `spin` (deg/s: how fast it turns in the world, from its
rotation every frame; docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5); `world_yaw` and `world_pitch` (degrees in (-180, 180]: a scene
component's own rotation in the world, angles like `yaw`, so `to_angle` and `to_axis` apply; actors'
`world_yaw:<Component>` for a component selected by where or what it is rather than by a name). `intensity`, `extent_*`, `bounds_change`, `pose_change`, `glow` and `spin`
depend on what a build chose, so their threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal
(tools/validate-game.py).
ComponentsMeasure.title: ComponentsMeasure

Cursor.description: The mouse cursor moved to a viewport point (fractions 0-1); a following LeftMouseButton press clicks there.
Cursor.title: Cursor

Damage.description:
`damage` points dealt through the engine's own damage call (UGameplayStatics::ApplyPointDamage, which calls the
actor's TakeDamage and its OnTakeAnyDamage and OnTakePointDamage events) to the actor `to` selects nearest to the
player pawn (`{"player": true}`: the pawn), struck from the actor `from` selects nearest to it (default: the pawn,
or, when the pawn is struck, the nearest other pawn), whose controller is the instigator. For a game that takes
damage through the engine (a game with its own hit function is staged by its own controls and `pin`). What the
target's TakeDamage returned is its `damage_taken`: in a game made under the factories' contract, where TakeDamage
returns the damage actually applied, the read for what a hit did; in an older game a convention of its override,
never a check's only read (read a start-named `prop:` there). No target is a miss the play reports.
Damage.title: Damage

DrawnMeasure.description:
What is drawn in a place, whatever draws it (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.19): every primitive drawn in game within the place
(`near` a point, its height band applied; or within `radius` of a `line`), rendered alone, each pixel kept where
its depth puts it inside the place. Near a point: `drawn` (1 when anything is), `motion` (the share of what is drawn
there that changed since the previous sample: a moving mesh, particles, a panned material), `base_r|g|b` (the mean
rendered base colour, linear 0-1) and `base_change` (that colour's distance from the first sample's). Along a line:
`drawn`, `reach` (cm from `from` to the furthest point drawn on it) and `length` (cm of it drawn). Every field but
`drawn` depends on what a build drew, so its threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal
(tools/validate-game.py).
DrawnMeasure.title: DrawnMeasure

FileExists.description: At least `min_count` project files match `glob` (relative to the project; e.g. Content/Maps/*.umap).
FileExists.title: FileExists

GroundMeasure.description:
The ground (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.17): where a trace straight down meets it first (pawns aside; with `select`, only an actor
it matches counts), at a point `xy` [x, y] (`height`, z in cm; `hit`, 1 when it met anything) or over a box `box`
[x0, y0, x1, y1] sampled on a `grid` x `grid` lattice (`min`, `max`, `mean` of the heights, `range` = max - min,
the relief; `hits`). `range`'s threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
GroundMeasure.title: GroundMeasure

Has.description:
A component the actor carries (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.4): it matches when one of its own components matches every key given:
`class` (the component's class or a parent, as a components select names it), `lit` (it gives off light, as the
components `lit` field reads it), `visible` (drawn, as the components `visible` field reads it), `near` (the
component's own place within `radius` cm of a point), `simulating` (a primitive simulating physics), `movable`
(a scene component of Movable mobility): an object a player can shove (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.4).
Has.title: Has

Judge.description:
The game judge's question over evidence the grader takes itself (screenshots and gameplay frames of a scripted
play, and the brief), item by item; never the agent's own words. `before`: the grader also plays the game as it
was at the start, and the judge compares (a seeded task that changes how the game looks or plays). `route`: a
project file in which the agent leaves inputs that play its game through (the probe's [{t, key, press}], e.g.
Tests/win_route.json); the grader plays it in its own clean copy as one more play, and the judge is told when
the file is missing or isn't a route. `plays`: the task's own scripted plays the screenshots are taken in (a
probe's TaskPlay: its map, flags and inputs), instead of the grader's idle look and its drive, which every task
shares and which never press a task's own keys or leave a game's title screen; each is played on every side the
check shows (the developer's game, the start on a `before` check, the reference on a `reference` check). `shots`:
how many screenshots of each of its plays it is shown (5 unless said), spread evenly over the play, so a short play
with many is a run of frames a quarter of a second apart in which motion shows (an ease or a cut, feet that slide, a
trail); its plays times its shots are a judge's 20 at most.
Judge.title: Judge

Key.description: A key pressed or released (Unreal key names: W, SpaceBar, LeftMouseButton).
Key.title: Key

Line.description: A segment from `from` to `to` (points), and how far from it (`radius`, cm) counts as on it.
Line.title: Line

LogAbsent.description: No line of the game's log during a boot matches `pattern` (a regular expression).
LogAbsent.title: LogAbsent

LogMeasure.description: Lines of the play's game log matching `pattern`.
LogMeasure.title: LogMeasure

Move.description:
The mouse moved by `move` [dx, dy] pixels (right, down), spread evenly over `over` seconds (at once without it),
through Slate as a mouse's moves are: while the game viewport holds the mouse captured (mouse look, a game-only
input mode) the engine gets MouseX = dx, MouseY = -dy and Mouse2D; otherwise only the cursor moves, which the play
reports as a miss (probes.md 2m). To put the cursor on a point, use a cursor input.
Move.title: Move

Near.description:
Within `radius` cm of `point`; `z_min`/`z_max` (cm) also keep it within a height band: world z, or offsets from
the point's z with `z_relative` (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.13).
Near.title: Near

Package.description: A Development package builds, and the packaged game boots.
Package.title: Package

PieceSelect.description:
Placed mesh pieces (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.14): of mesh components of a class (StaticMeshComponent, which takes in the
instanced ones, InstancedStaticMeshComponent, ProceduralMeshComponent; default every mesh component), optionally by
the component's name, its mesh asset's name (`mesh`, a wildcard), an owner actor the `owner` select matches, and
near a point (each piece by its own place).
PieceSelect.title: PieceSelect

PiecesMeasure.description:
Placed mesh pieces, whatever their form (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.14): a mesh component with a mesh is one, an instanced one
one per instance, a procedural mesh one per section; counted over all of them, never cut at the rows cap.
`triangles`/`visible_triangles`: the triangles those pieces (those drawn) hold; they depend on the meshes a build
chose, so their threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
PiecesMeasure.title: PiecesMeasure

Pin.description:
The actor `pin` selects nearest to the player pawn (never the pawn itself) held at its place for `hold` seconds
of play, put back after every tick of the world with its movement stopped while its own logic runs on (it still
turns, swings, blocks, opens its shutters); with `front`, first set that many cm ahead of the pawn along the pawn's
facing (plus `offset`, cm), at the height above the ground it had, turned to face the pawn: a target or an opponent
where the player's blow or shot lands, whatever place a build gave it; with `at`, first set at that point (plus
`offset`), facing the pawn: next to what the player threw or dropped (a flare that landed). A pin no actor matches,
or whose point doesn't resolve, is a miss the play reports.
Pin.title: Pin

Probe.description:
A deterministic check (docs/task-probes.md): `measure` taken where `play` says, reduced to one number, compared with
`expect`. `describe` is the assertion in plain English, shown in the grade.
Probe.title: Probe

ScreenMeasure.description:
The frame the player sees (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.15): mean luminance of the drawn frame, after post-processing, over `rect`
[x0, y0, x1, y1] in viewport fractions (default the whole frame). It moves between machines, so its threshold is
calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
ScreenMeasure.title: ScreenMeasure

Seed.description:
Where a seeded task starts: one of the studio's games at `commit`. `game` is its slug: the game's repository
(game-<slug>) and its folder under the machine's games root.
`reference`: a later commit of that game whose change solves the task (a bug's fix), for calibrated probes, the code judge and the task check.
`history`: which history the two commits are from: "private", the game's own repository (its clone,
GitHub, a mirror), or "dataset", the rewritten history a layout v1.3 Dataset.zip delivers (History/), whose
commit ids differ; the game's commit map translates either way.
Seed.title: Seed

Select.description:
Actors that match every key given: `class` (the actor's class or a parent, without prefix letters; a Blueprint
class by its asset name, BP_Wall_C), `tag` (an actor tag), `name` (a wildcard on its name or label), `near`
(within `radius` cm of a point), `player` (the player pawn), `has` (a component it carries that matches every key
given there: an actor that gives light, one with a drawn mesh near a point).
Select.title: Select

SetProp.description:
A reflected property (the path a prop: field reads, no array index) written on the actor `on` selects nearest to
the player pawn, or on every match with `all`: a number, a boolean, or an enum, name or string by its text; for a
property the task's start already has (a revenant's Health at 1, so one blow fells it through the game's own death;
the player's own high, so a staged fight can't end the play). A set no actor or no property takes is a miss the
play reports.
SetProp.title: SetProp

Shot.description:
A screenshot at `t` with the UI, as the player sees it, named `shot` (shot_<name>.png beside the evenly spaced
ones): the grader's own picture of a moment, for a judge and for whoever reviews a run (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1). Never a pass
or fail by itself.
Shot.title: Shot

StartPlus.description: Threshold s + d: the start (s) measured in the grading environment (a task with no developers' fix).
StartPlus.title: StartPlus

StartTimes.description: Threshold s * f: the start (s) measured in the grading environment (a task with no developers' fix).
StartTimes.title: StartTimes

TaskPlay.description:
A task-defined scripted play: `inputs` (keys, axes, widget clicks, wheel notches, mouse movement, ...; and the
grader's stages of a contact: pin, damage, set) sent at their times during `seconds` (a move spread over time
ends by then too); its
own `map` (with URL options) instead of the task's play_map, `args` on its command line (game flags, -Name or
-Name=value, but never the grader's own: DENIED_ARGS, -GameEnv*), and samples every `every` seconds (default
0.5). `after`: the task plays (probe or judge plays of the task) that run and end on the same side before it
starts, for a play that reads what another writes (a save: a side's plays share the game's Saved folder); one that
failed still counts as run.
TaskPlay.title: TaskPlay

Teleport.description:
The player pawn placed at `teleport` (cm) facing `yaw`: the grader's own way to reach a test spot; `hold`: for
that many seconds of play the pawn is put back there after every tick of the world, for a game that sets its
player's place every tick (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
Teleport.title: Teleport

TeleportTo.description:
The player pawn placed next to the actor `teleport_to` selects nearest to it (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1): `distance` cm from
it on the pawn's side, level with it, plus `offset` (cm), facing `face` (a point) or else that actor; for a spot a
build chose itself (an ore it placed). Nothing happens when no actor matches. `hold`: as a teleport's, the pawn
kept at that spot for that many seconds of play (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
TeleportTo.title: TeleportTo

TraceMeasure.description: A fact of the agent's own trace (never gating).
TraceMeasure.title: TraceMeasure

Travel.description:
At `t` the play opens another map (with URL options: another scenario), as the game's own travel does; its clock
runs on through the load, and inputs and samples wait for the new world's player (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1). With shots and
teleports, one launch visits several places and pictures each.
Travel.title: Travel

UiMeasure.description:
What the UI shows on screen, whatever draws it (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18): the elements on screen in the frame drawn right
after each sample, from UMG widgets, Slate widgets and the HUD canvas (AHUD DrawText, DrawRect, DrawTexture,
DrawLine, K2_DrawBox and the canvas's other draws) alike, only what is drawn (a collapsed or hidden widget is not).
`count` (one per element), `text` (with `match`; digits drawn as seven-segment strokes read as text too, and a
select of text with a `rect` also reads the frame as drawn there, however the text was drawn), `x`,
`y`, `w`, `h` (its rectangle in viewport fractions); `of` combines the elements `select` picks. `signature`: one
value a sample for everything the select picks (kinds, texts, rectangles), read with `agg` `changes` (how many
samples show something other than the one before: a readout that updates, however it is drawn), `any`, `all` or
`count` (samples showing anything); `of` is ignored (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18). `number`: the first number its text elements
show, in reading order; `clock`: the first time they show (h:mm:ss, m:ss, or else a number, as seconds); read with
`rises`, `falls`, `changes` or `range` for which way it moved, `of` ignored (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18). The way to check what a
HUD shows, however a build drew it.
UiMeasure.title: UiMeasure

UiSelect.description:
Which of the UI elements on screen (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18): `kind` (text, box, image, line), `text` (a regular expression
the element's text must match; text elements only) and `rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1] in viewport fractions (the element's
centre inside); none: every element on screen.
UiSelect.title: UiSelect

Value.description: A literal threshold, for facts that don't depend on the scene (counts, booleans).
Value.title: Value

View.description:
At `t` the player's view turns to `view` [pitch, yaw] in degrees (the control rotation; pitch -89 to 89), for a
shot that faces a given way (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
View.title: View

Wait.description:
At `t` the play's clock holds for `wait` seconds of real time while the game runs on, paced to real time (each
frame waits for the wall clock to catch up with the game's own time), for what runs on the wall clock (a menu that
pages on real time). No samples, inputs or screenshots meanwhile; then the play goes on from `t` (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
Wait.title: Wait

Wheel.description:
Mouse wheel notches at the cursor (the viewport's centre before any cursor move), positive away from the player
(scroll up), sent through Slate as a wheel's are: the UI under the cursor or the game viewport takes them, which
gives the engine's MouseWheelAxis and MouseScrollUp/MouseScrollDown, to legacy mappings and Enhanced Input alike
(probes.md 2m). A wheel no game viewport receives is a miss the play reports.
Wheel.title: Wheel

Where.description:
A reflected property of the actor (the path a prop: field reads) compared with a value: a number, a boolean (1
or 0) or a string (docs/planning/2026-11-11_game-contact-checks/spec.md); an actor whose property doesn't resolve
doesn't match.
Where.title: Where

WidgetSelect.description:
Widgets on screen: UMG widgets in the viewport by their class (WBP_HUD_C, TextBlock) and/or name, or Slate
widgets under the game viewport by their type (`slate`: STextBlock, SImage, a game's own S... type); `text`: a
regular expression the widget's text must match; `visible`: only the widgets drawn (as the `visible` field reads
them: never a collapsed or hidden one, nor one under such a parent), so a select counts what is on screen.
WidgetSelect.title: WidgetSelect

WorldMeasure.description:
The game world as a whole (game-contact-checks spec): `time_dilation`, the lowest global time dilation over the
frames since the previous sample (a hit pause made by slowing the world, however short: 1 when the world ran at
its pace); `paused`, 1 when the game was paused in any of those frames ("Escape pauses the game").
WorldMeasure.title: WorldMeasure

template.description: Read past: every task starts from its seed (2026-10-18).
template.title: Template

title: game-task/1
